newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police held in Elf Gabon probe theft.
newsitem.headline: Police held in Elf Gabon probe theft.

text.p: Four French financial police officers were placed under police guard on Friday in a probe into the disappearance of documents linking a Swiss bank account held by Elf Aquitaine oil company with Gabon President Omar Bongo.
The documents, which were under seal, disappeared from financial police headquarters last weekend.
Police sources said Paris judge Eva Joly had been using them as part of her ultra-sensitive investigation into the oil firm's activities in the West African state.
The officers were released during the evening, France Info radio reported.

The CGT union's police branch said the four were detained by the IGS police inspection service. It condemned the decision, saying it raised suspicions that they were guilty, and called for their immediate release.
The four officers were charged by Joly with seizing the documents at the home of a Saint-Tropez decorator late last week and with exploiting them.

The chairman of Elf's Gabon subsidiary, Andre Tarallo, is under judicial investigation in France on suspicion of receiving the proceeds of misuse of corporate funds. He is currently free on 10 million francs ($1.8 million) bail.
Judicial sources have said Tarallo told Joly he opened a bank account in Switzerland that was used solely by Bongo.
Joly is investigating alleged fraud at Elf involving the payment of alleged covert commissions while former French railways chief Loic Le Floch-Prigent was chairman from 1988 to 1993.
She placed Le Floch-Prigent in preventive detention last year but he was released in December after six months.
